enforcement.transport: mutual TLS with required client authentication
enforcement.identity: replica-{id} certificate common-name binding to RPC identity
enforcement.attestation: mandatory externally supplied verifier; default daemon entrypoint denies
enforcement.record_signatures: mandatory externally supplied verifier; default daemon entrypoint denies
enforcement.election: monotonic term, one vote per term, journal freshness and chain-root checks
enforcement.journal: bounded records, bounded payloads, contiguous sequence, previous-digest and record-digest validation
enforcement.persistence: checksummed atomic JSON state, fsync, atomic replace, directory fsync, mode 0600
enforcement.commit: leader commit is capped at the durable follower match sequence

tests.mutual_tls_grpc_round_trip: vote and append passed with ephemeral CA and replica certificates

limitations: The daemon is not yet wired to the C election library; the Python runtime maintains its own bounded durable term/vote state and must be reconciled before production packaging.
The command-line entrypoint intentionally installs rejecting verifiers until a trusted attestation/signature provider is explicitly provisioned.
InstallSnapshot remains fail-closed and unimplemented pending a verified snapshot store.
No claim is made for live AWS KMS/Vault credentials, physical TPM/secure enclave, production certificate rotation, or multi-node deployment qualification.
The TLS test uses ephemeral local certificates and is not hardware or production PKI evidence.
